task_description: Build the Taskboard UI server: Node.js 24, TypeScript, Express 5 with EJS server-rendered pages (login, register, forgot/reset password, dashboard, team page, project board, task detail, search, profile, admin users, admin activity). It authenticates browser users by storing the API's opaque session token in an HttpOnly SameSite cookie and calls the internal API with Authorization: Bearer plus a shared service secret header; CSRF protection with an HMAC token bound to a cookie on every POST form; flash messages in a signed cookie; renders task descriptions and comments written in Markdown to HTML (marked) and sanitizes them (sanitize-html); proxies multipart attachment uploads (multer, 10 MB limit) and streams downloads back with Content-Disposition attachment; strict CSP via helmet; structured JSON logging with a per-request id passed to the API; post-login redirect to a local path.

An uploaded archive writes files outside the target folder when extracted
Sensitive data travels over plain HTTP or an unencrypted connection
Debug features or consoles are left on in production

.env, .git, or backup files are reachable from the web
Forged or unsigned JWTs are accepted
Long-lived storage keys are shipped to the browser or mobile app
A request sets fields the user should not control, such as role or price
One user reads or changes another user's data by changing an id in the request
Session ids, reset tokens, or API keys can be guessed
An attacker plants a session id before login and reuses it afterwards
Attacker-supplied content is shown to other users as HTML or script
Attacker uploads a script that your server runs or serves

A user skips or repeats steps in a multi-step flow, such as verification or checkout
Another website makes a logged-in user's browser perform actions

countermeasures.name: Check permissions on the server for every action
countermeasures.how_to: Enforce role and permission checks in a central layer on each endpoint, not only by hiding UI.

countermeasures.name: Extract archives safely
countermeasures.how_to: Ignore paths inside archives, reject symlinks and entries that escape the target folder, and cap size and file count.

countermeasures.name: Use HTTPS for every connection
countermeasures.how_to: Serve everything over HTTPS with a trusted certificate, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, and use TLS for service-to-service calls as well.

countermeasures.name: Turn debug features off in production
countermeasures.how_to: Set DEBUG false, remove debug consoles and verbose logging, and fail the deploy if debug is on.

countermeasures.name: Use safe DOM APIs
countermeasures.how_to: Use textContent or framework bindings instead of innerHTML, document.write, or dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

countermeasures.name: Encode output for its context
countermeasures.how_to: Use your template engine's automatic escaping, and encode correctly for HTML, attributes, URLs, and JavaScript.

countermeasures.name: Do not deploy repo metadata or env files
countermeasures.how_to: Exclude .git, .env, and backups from the build and the web root, and block them at the web server.

countermeasures.name: Load secrets from a secrets manager or environment
countermeasures.how_to: Keep secrets out of code, images, and the repo. Use environment variables or a vault, scope access narrowly, and rotate anything that leaked.

countermeasures.name: Verify token signatures against an allow-list of algorithms
countermeasures.how_to: Verify every JWT signature, fix the accepted algorithms in code, and load keys from trusted configuration. Never accept alg none.

countermeasures.name: Give clients short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials
countermeasures.how_to: Issue pre-signed or token-exchanged credentials limited to one object or prefix. Never ship long-lived keys to clients.

countermeasures.name: Accept only the fields you expect
countermeasures.how_to: Bind requests to an explicit schema or DTO with allowed fields. Never copy a request body straight onto a model.

countermeasures.name: Check the user owns the object on every request
countermeasures.how_to: Look the object up by id AND owner, or check ownership explicitly, and return 404 when they do not match.

countermeasures.name: Generate tokens with a cryptographic random source
countermeasures.how_to: Use secrets.token_urlsafe, crypto.randomBytes, or the framework default. Never use Math.random, time, or counters.

countermeasures.name: Issue a fresh session at login
countermeasures.how_to: Create a new session id on every login and re-authentication, and discard the old one.

countermeasures.name: Sanitize user-provided HTML
countermeasures.how_to: Run user HTML through a maintained sanitizer such as DOMPurify or bleach with a strict allow-list. Prefer markdown or plain text.

countermeasures.name: Allow only the file types you need
countermeasures.how_to: Check the extension and the real file content against an allow-list. Ignore the client's Content-Type.

countermeasures.name: Never use the user's filename or path
countermeasures.how_to: Generate your own filenames, store files outside the web root, and make sure uploads are never executed.

countermeasures.name: Enforce step order and limits on the server
countermeasures.how_to: Store the state of multi-step flows on the server and reject steps that are out of order. Apply business limits there too.

countermeasures.name: Protect state-changing requests from cross-site forgery
countermeasures.how_to: Use SameSite cookies plus anti-forgery tokens, and only change state with POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE.

countermeasures.name: Set cookie security attributes
countermeasures.how_to: Use Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite on session cookies, preferably with the __Host- prefix.

countermeasures.name: Return only the fields the client needs
countermeasures.how_to: Build response objects from an explicit list of fields instead of serializing whole database rows.

countermeasures.name: Validate all input on the server
countermeasures.how_to: Check type, length, range, and format for every input on the server. Client-side checks are only for convenience.

countermeasures.name: Rate-limit expensive or sensitive endpoints
countermeasures.how_to: Limit requests per user and per IP on login, reset, send, upload, and search endpoints, and return 429 when exceeded.

countermeasures.name: Redirect only to known destinations
countermeasures.how_to: Accept a short key or a relative path for post-login redirects and check it against an allow-list. Never redirect to a full URL from input.

countermeasures.name: Allow only the origins you trust
countermeasures.how_to: Return a fixed allow-list for Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Never reflect the request origin or use * with credentials.

countermeasures.name: End sessions on the server
countermeasures.how_to: Invalidate server-side on logout, expiry, password change, and account removal. Do not rely on deleting the cookie client-side.

countermeasures.name: Pin third-party scripts with integrity hashes
countermeasures.how_to: Add SRI hashes to external scripts and styles, or self-host them, and limit sources with a Content-Security-Policy.

countermeasures.name: Send the standard security headers
countermeasures.how_to: Set Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy with frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and a referrer policy.

countermeasures.name: Check expiry, audience, and issuer
countermeasures.how_to: Reject expired tokens and tokens whose audience or issuer does not match your service.

countermeasures.name: Keep tokens and personal data out of URLs
countermeasures.how_to: Send tokens in headers or request bodies, never in query strings, which end up in logs and referrers.

countermeasures.name: Keep sensitive data out of browser storage
countermeasures.how_to: Prefer HttpOnly cookies for session tokens, and clear client-side data on logout.

countermeasures.name: Serve uploads so browsers cannot run them
countermeasures.how_to: Send the correct Content-Type, Content-Disposition attachment for downloads, nosniff, and serve user files from a separate domain.

countermeasures.name: Limit file size and decompressed size
countermeasures.how_to: Set a maximum size per file, and cap decompressed size and file count for archives.

countermeasures.name: Return generic errors to users
countermeasures.how_to: Show a short message and a request id, log the details server-side, and use the same wording for unknown and wrong credentials.

assessment.summary: 31 threats and 34 countermeasures for browser-frontend, user-generated-content, session-management, web-endpoint, file-upload. Risk level critical (highest threat severity, raised for sensitive data).

instructions: Build these countermeasures in as you write the code, starting with the most severe threats. These threats come from the components you picked. also_consider lists general threats from implied components; pass those components explicitly for full detail. After writing code, call general_verify_code_security with the same components.
